nodes.label: argocd-image-updater Resource Rightsizing
nodes.rationale: argocd-image-updater is installed from upstream install.yaml and not otherwise GitOps-tracked. A strategic-merge patch trims its default requests/limits (250m/512Mi request, 500m/1Gi limit) down toward observed actual usage of ~3m CPU / ~33Mi memory.

nodes.label: Liveness vs Readiness Probe Split for Kafka Consumer Health
nodes.norm_label: liveness vs readiness probe split for kafka consumer health
nodes.rationale: /health always returns 200 regardless of internal state, so kafka_consumer_running could sit false for hours undetected (2026-09-27 incident, docs/Chuseok-Power-Outage-Recovery.md). /live returns 503 when kafka_consumer_running is false, which lets the kubelet restart the pod. livenessProbe was repointed from /health to /live to fix this.

nodes.label: Multi-source Live Feed Fusion (ADS-B + AIS)
nodes.rationale: ADSB_ENABLED (opendata.adsb.fi real-time public ADS-B feed) and AIS_ENABLED (aisstream.io real-time AIS/vessel WebSocket feed) are enabled together as a second real-time data source to demonstrate a multi-source fusion architecture, directly addressing the 'single modality' limitation called out in docs/MSS-Comparison-and-Asset-Recommendation-Engine.md. Changing the center coordinates repurposes surveillance to other regions (e.g. Ukraine/Iran) per application.yaml.

nodes.rationale: Changed from daily to hourly cron (max detection delay 24h -> 1h) after the home-server Mac mini silently dropped off Tailscale overnight and was only discovered a day later on the next scheduled run.

nodes.label: ntfy.sh Push Alert
nodes.rationale: Added ntfy.sh push notification alongside GitHub's default email alert because push is noticed much faster while away from a computer. ntfy is signup-free and topic-based (anyone who knows NTFY_TOPIC can subscribe/publish), so the exposed topic name was deliberately chosen as a hard-to-guess random string to act as a de facto secret despite the public repo.

nodes.label: 2GB Swap OOM Defense
nodes.rationale: Each node's physical RAM (1-2GB) is too small to survive memory spikes without pods being OOM-killed, so a permanent 2GB swap partition is registered in /etc/fstab on every node to eliminate that downtime.

nodes.label: Deliberate k3s-master Placement
nodes.rationale: This cluster's usual convention is to avoid scheduling on the control plane, but both workers already sit at ~74% memory (per docs/concepts/09-swarm-load-generator-design-discussion.md item 7, where resource contention on those exact nodes previously caused outages), while the master has more free CPU/RAM. Since GitNexus indexing is memory-heavy, the convention was deliberately broken to place it on k3s-master instead.

nodes.label: Memory Limit Raised 1Gi -> 2Gi
nodes.rationale: Started at a 1Gi memory limit, but `gitnexus group sync` (opening 3 repos simultaneously for contract extraction and cross-linking) was observed to be OOMKilled; single-repo analyze/auto-sync uses less memory than group sync. Raised to 2Gi, staying under the master's available memory headroom (~1.2GB at the time of this decision).

nodes.label: GITNEXUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN Deliberately Omitted
nodes.rationale: A local smoke test confirmed that setting GITNEXUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN with a wildcard bind (--host 0.0.0.0) makes gitnexus serve refuse to start, warning that it has no authentication yet and must be reached through an authenticating proxy. So the variable isn't optionally left out -- it cannot be set without breaking startup. As a consequence, write routes (POST /api/analyze, DELETE /api/repo) only accept loopback origins by default, so indexing via NodePort/Tailscale works for viewing the graph but the UI's index button may be blocked; recommended workaround is kubectl exec (run CLI in-pod) or kubectl port-forward to localhost.

nodes.label: Secret Volume defaultMode 0444
nodes.rationale: Secret volumes mount as root-owned, but the container runs as USER node (UID 1000), so the default 0400 (owner-read-only) mode leaves node unable to read the key. SSH's own permission check only rejects group/other write bits, not read bits, so defaultMode is relaxed to 0444 (world-readable, no write bits) so node can read it without violating ssh's strictness check.

nodes.label: ssh-agent Per-Repo Deploy Keys
nodes.rationale: Each repo uses its own dedicated deploy key (GitHub rejects registering the same key as a deploy key on multiple repos), but all repos are on github.com so per-host IdentityFile selection doesn't work. Instead of pinning -i, the entrypoint's ssh-agent loads every key and picks the right one per repo automatically. SSH_AUTH_SOCK is declared as a pod env var so any exec session (e.g. manual auto-sync) can reach the same agent socket. known_hosts is kept on the PVC (/data) so it persists across restarts and doesn't need to re-TOFU.

nodes.label: local-path Storage Tied to nodeAffinity
nodes.rationale: GITNEXUS_HOME (/data/.gitnexus) holds per-repo graph indexes and registry.json on local-path storage, which is node-local. This must match the nodeAffinity in deployment.yaml that pins the pod to k3s-master, or moving to another node would make the PV invisible.

nodes.label: NodePort Chosen Over Ingress
nodes.rationale: This cluster's Traefik Ingress is exposed to the whole public internet via Tailscale Funnel (see docs/Public-Access-via-Tailscale-Funnel.md), so routing gitnexus through Ingress would turn an 'internal-only' tool into a globally public one. NodePort bypasses Funnel and is reachable only within the tailnet, making it the genuinely internal-only pattern -- the same one used for Headlamp/Grafana/Prometheus.
